status: Pilot, written by Claude on 12 November 2026 and not yet checked by the translation workers. Informal jij throughout.

lessons.title: Sounds and Script - The Dutch G, Part 1
lessons.description: G and ch are a soft scrape at the back of the throat. Hear it in goed, groot, acht, and lachen.

lessons.title: Sounds and Script - Long and Short Vowels, Part 1
lessons.description: A doubled vowel is long, and it changes the word. Hear man against maan, and bom against boom.

lessons.title: Sounds and Script - Ui and Ij, Part 1
lessons.description: Two sounds English does not have: the ui of huis, and the ij of tijd. Listen closely to huis, uit, tijd, and ijs.

lessons.title: Sounds and Script - Spelling Follows the Sound, Part 1
lessons.description: When a word grows, its spelling changes to keep the vowel long or short: maan becomes manen, and man becomes mannen.

lessons.title: Patterns - To Go in the Present, Part 1
lessons.description: The verb gaan, to go, changes to say who is going. Spot what changes: ga, gaat, gaat, gaan.

lessons.title: Patterns - To Go in the Present, Part 2
lessons.description: More of gaan, to go: for all of you, for them, for "let's", and for what you are about to do.

lessons.title: Patterns - More Than One, Part 1
lessons.description: Most words add en for more than one, and every one of them takes de, even a word that takes het when it is alone.

lessons.title: Patterns - Two Words for The, Part 1
lessons.description: Every naming word takes de or het, and it is learned with the word. Small things ending in je always take het: het meisje.

lessons.title: Sentence Building - Asking a Question, Part 1
lessons.description: To ask a question, the verb moves to the front of the sentence.
words: This is the bus to Amsterdam.
Dit is de bus naar Amsterdam.
Is this the bus to Amsterdam?
Is dit de bus naar Amsterdam?

lessons.title: Sentence Building - Saying No, Part 1
lessons.description: The word niet says not. It comes after the verb, and often at the very end.

lessons.title: Sentence Building - The Verb Comes Second, Part 1
lessons.description: In a plain statement, the verb is always the second piece of the sentence. Start with today, and I has to move behind the verb.

lessons.title: Sentence Building - Describing Words Come First, Part 1
lessons.description: As in English, the describing word comes before the thing. Most gain an e: zwarte, grote. After een, before a het word, they do not: een wit huis.

lessons.title: Sentences in Use - Going Places, Part 1
lessons.description: The verb gaan, to go, at work in whole sentences. Spot ga, gaan, and the verb moving to the front for a question.
words: I am going to the market.
We are going to the beach.
Are you going to the party?

lessons.title: Sentences in Use - Questions and Answers, Part 1
lessons.description: A question and its answer, side by side. Before a thing, not becomes geen, so Dutch says I speak no English: ik spreek geen Engels.
words: No, I do not speak English.

lessons.title: Sentences in Use - Describing Things, Part 1
lessons.description: After is and zijn, the describing word takes no ending at all: wit, rood, lang, klein.

lessons.title: Sentences in Use - Yesterday, Today, and Tomorrow, Part 1
lessons.description: One trip to the market, told three ways. Watch the verb keep its second place every time.
words: I went to the market yesterday.
Gisteren ging ik naar de markt.
I am going to the market today.
Vandaag ga ik naar de markt.
I will go to the market tomorrow.
Morgen zal ik naar de markt gaan.
